description: MECHANISM: an assignment's VALUE is a read and is judged like any other (issue #1155). Measured before this fixture existed: suppressing the check of assignment values left the whole unit suite and the full fixture corpus green, yet is behaviour-changing — on the pre-#1155 evaluator `set n to repcount` raises `ol-repcount-outside-repeat` at `runtime` after 1 event, so the mutant restores partial execution in place of semantic refusal. Nothing walled it, because the corpus asserted only the CLEAN direction (`repeat 2 [ set n to repcount ]`, which stays silent under the mutant too). A clean-direction assertion covers a rule's silence, not the rule. Note `:n = repcount` is the SAME mechanism, not a second one: both parse to `Assign` with a `Place` target and a `Call` value, differing only in `form` (`"set"` versus `"equals"`), so a twin fixture would count one mechanism twice. Its pair is the assignment TARGET, which is not a read — `core-language/assignment/bare-place-invalid`.
